title: Tenant-aware SLOs and Cost Prioritization Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a repeatable, cross-functional process for setting, operating, and reviewing tenant-aware SLOs that explicitly incorporate cost impact and multi-tenant prioritization. It ties SLOs to error budgets and capacity actions so that incident decisions consider both reliability and unit economics for Redwood’s inference services.

Intended audience

- SREs owning inference services and multi-tenant routing
- Product & platform PMs who set customer tiers and monetization rules
- Oncall engineers performing triage and runbook actions
- Finance/Cost ops teams interested in cost/reliability tradeoffs

Principles and goals

1. Surface tradeoffs: SLO design should make reliability vs cost explicit at the tenant level (e.g., free/standard/premium).
2. Error budgets are the primary control-plane for automated capacity and rate-limiting actions.
3. Make mitigation decisions observable and reversible (audit log for budget spend and throttles).
4. Minimize customer-blind mitigations: prefer tier-aware graceful degradation over global throttles.
5. Post-incident reviews must quantify both reliability and cost impact.

Scope and responsibilities

- SRE: owns SLO definitions, alerting, automated budget enforcement rules, and runbook steps.
- Platform PM: defines tier behavior and acceptable degradation modes.
- Finance: provides unit-cost models for inference tokens/requests to inform prioritization.
- Account success: approves customer communication templates for degradations.

SLO taxonomy (examples)

| SLO name | Unit | Target | Owner | Tier applicability | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| inference_99_latency | p95 request latency (ms) | 200ms | inference-sre | premium,standard | Separate p50/p95/p99 for analytics
| inference_request_success | request success ratio | 99.95% | inference-sre | all tiers | Includes transient 5xx + model OOMs
| embeddings_avg_cost | $ per 1k vectors | <= $X | platform-cost | internal metric | Used for cost-guardrails and autoscale triggers

Design patterns for tenant-aware SLOs

- Tiered SLOs: Define a baseline SLO for all tenants, stronger SLOs for paid tiers. Use the same metric definitions to keep tooling consistent.
- Progressive degradation: For sustained capacity pressure, degrade lower tiers first by (1) reducing max tokens, (2) lowering model variant (quantized/cheaper), (3) increasing batching window.
- Soft limits and hard failovers: Soft limits trigger routing and QoS changes; hard failovers are reserved for safety-critical events.

Automated enforcement and tooling

- Error-budget controller: A service that consumes SLO telemetry, maintains per-tenant error budget state, and exposes actions: throttle, route-to-cheaper, notify.
- Enforcement policy format (YAML example):

policy: tenant_priority_policy
rules:
  - name: degrade-lower-tier
    when: error_budget.spent > 0.6 AND capacity_utilization > 0.75
    action: route_to_compatible_model
    params:
      max_tiers: [standard, free]
  - name: emergency-throttle
    when: error_budget.spent > 0.9 AND tail_latency > 500ms
    action: per-tenant-rate-limit
    params:
      allow: 10rps

(Implementation note: controller should emit audit events for each action with tenant-id, rule-id, reason, and triggering metric values.)

Runbook: live incident triage (high-level)

1. Detect: Pager triggers for either SLO alert or cost anomaly (cost ops alert).
2. Triage: Identify whether impact is tenant-scoped or global, and whether error budgets are the root cause or symptom.
3. Contain: If global and high utilization, follow prioritized mitigations:
   a. Disable non-critical background jobs (platform ops).
   b. Route lower-tier traffic to cheaper model variants.
   c. Turn on per-tenant circuit-breakers for top offenders.
4. Stabilize: Engage capacity autoscale for reserved pools, open temporary burst capacity if contracts allow.
5. Communicate: Use pre-approved templates. Classify incident as: degradation/partial outage/major outage. Notify affected tenants based on tier.
6. Post-incident: Start RCA and schedule postmortem with cost quantification.

Detailed triage checklist (for oncall)

- Identify the alert source and exact SLO metric.
- Run queries:
  - per_tenant_success_rate(last_1h), top 10 tenants by error rate
  - cluster_gpu_utilization(last_15m), queue_depths, pending_batches
  - model_variant_failures and OOM traces
- Decision gating: If top 3 tenants account for >60% of errors and are lower-tier, consider selective throttle.
- If autoscale failed to provision nodes: escalate to infra-sre and open cloud provisioning runbook.

Capacity planning interactions

- Forecast inputs: tenant growth forecasts (product), historical per-tenant qps and token distribution (telemetry), planned model rollouts (research).
- Capacitor table (example):

| Period | Expected peak QPS | Buffer % | Reserved GPUs | Notes |
| Q4-2025 | 12,000 | 30% | 120 A100s | holiday promotions expected |
| Q1-2026 | 9,000 | 25% | 90 A100s | grad-school campaign ends |

- Run regular SLO-cost sync meetings (monthly) with finance and product to translate forecast into committed capacity and expected unit cost.

Reliability initiatives and experiments suggested

- Tenant-level chaos tests: periodically simulate a noisy-tenant scenario (traffic spike + malformed prompts) in staging with the same routing rules to validate tiered degradation logic.
- Cost-awareness experiments: A/B test reducing default max_tokens for free tier by 15% and measure error-budget consumption and revenue impact.
- Admission control heuristics: experiment with adaptive batch windows that increase batching for cheap tenants when utilization > threshold.

Incident review standards (postmortem requirements)

Every post-incident review that touches an SLO must include:
- Timeline of events with telemetry links (start/stop of mitigations and controller actions).
- Error budget burn rate and remaining budget by tenant at 10m resolution.
- Cost impact analysis: incremental $ spend for burst capacity, estimated revenue at risk during degradation window.
- Root cause and contributing factors (human, infra, model).
- Action items tagged with owners and SLA for remediation.

Template excerpt (to paste into postmortem doc)

1. Incident summary (1–3 sentences)
2. Detection and scope (alerts, coverage, tenants affected)
3. Impact matrix (SLO breaches, customer-facing errors, cost delta)
4. Timeline of mitigation actions and controller decisions
5. Root cause analysis
6. Remediation plan and verification checks

Telemetry and dashboards (minimum set)

- Per-tier SLO dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, success ratio, error budget remaining, budget burn rate.
- Top-ten tenants by error volume and cost (side-by-side chart).
- Enforcement audit stream: policy actions with timestamps and inputs.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens by model variant and region.

Alerting guidance

- SLO alerts: trigger on burn-rate and absolute breach windows (e.g., 14-day burn-rate > 1.5x and 1h breach count > threshold).
- Cost alerts: sudden unit-cost increase > 20% vs 24h followed by sustained >10% for 1h.
- Enforcement action alerts: when controller applies degrade/throttle to >5 tenants within 10m.

Communication templates (short)

- Degradation (standard tenants): "We are experiencing increased latency that may affect your requests. As we prioritize premium customers, you may observe slower responses or reduced max tokens until the situation is resolved. We expect recovery within X hours."
- Outage (premium customers): personalized status page entries and direct Slack/email with remediation ETA.

Verification and rollout checklist for SLO or enforcement policy changes

1. Define hypothesis and rollback criteria.
2. Small-scale test in staging with synthetic tenants.
3. Canary in production limited to 2–3 non-critical customers or a feature-flagged sample.
4. Monitor error budgets and cost signals for 48–72 hours.
5. Gradual rollout with automatic rollback on predefined triggers.

Appendix: example SLO configuration (JSON-friendly)

{\n  "slo_id": "inference_request_success::tier:standard",\n  "description": "Request success ratio for standard tier tenants",\n  "window": "30d",\n  "target": "0.9995",\n  "alerting": {"burn_rate_threshold": 1.5, "window_minutes": 60},\n  "enforcement_policy": "degrade-lower-tier"\n}

Appendix: audit and compliance notes

- All enforcement actions must be logged to the enforcement-audit topic and retained for 90 days.
- For customers with contractual SLAs, any automated action that changes their effective behavior for >10 minutes must be approved by oncall lead and recorded in the incident timeline.

Roadmap items and known limitations

- Integrate error-budget controller with cost forecasting to proactively spin reserves for expected billing events.
- Improve tenant-level forecasting with ML model that predicts token distribution per tenant 7 days out.
- Current limitation: per-tenant request tracing latency can reach 1s for large trace windows—plan to roll lightweight sampling.

Glossary

- Error budget: allowable slack for SLO violations before mitigations escalate.
- Degrade: intentional reduction of service quality (tokens, model variant) to preserve higher-tier SLOs.
- Enforcement controller: automated system that reads budgets and executes pre-authorized policy actions.

Contact and escalation

- Primary oncall: inference-sre rotation (see roster).
- Escalation path: oncall -> inference-sre lead -> infra-sre -> platform PM.

This playbook is a living document. Updates should be recorded in the page history and reviewed quarterly or after any SLO-affecting incident.
